title: Structural basis of the gating mechanism of the large-conductance mechanosensitive channel from Escherichia coli
task: Determine the gating mechanism of mechanosensitive channel MscL through high-resolution structures
key_results: Solved closed-state structures in DMPC/DOPC lipid nanodiscs and expanded-state structure in DSPC lipids; identified dynamics sites involved in closed-to-expanded transition via HDX-MS and MD simulations
comments: The lipid-dependent shift from closed to expanded states highlights the importance of membrane composition in mechanosensing, though the precise tension-sensing mechanism remains partially unresolved.

outputs: 3D structures in closed and expanded conformations

hypotheses.hypothesis: High-resolution structural information combined with spectroscopy would reveal the gating mechanism
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: identified closed-to-expanded transition sites and lipid-dependent state shifts

hypotheses.hypothesis: EcMscL undergoes tension-gated conformational changes from closed to expanded state
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: expanded state structure solved with pore properties consistent with electrophysiology

title: An additional water is introduced into the manganese cluster during the formation of the S3 state of photosystem II
task: Resolve the structural changes in the Mn4Ca cluster during S1-S3 state transitions and identify oxygen ligand insertion
key_results: High-resolution structures (~1.9 Å) confirm insertion of oxygen atom OX/O6 ligating to Mn1 and Ca in S3 state; OX-O5 distance of ~2.1 Å indicates weak interaction, suggesting O-O bond formation occurs during S3→S0 transition, not in S3
comments: Anomalous diffraction at two energies strengthens Mn positioning accuracy, but the functional significance of the weak OX-O5 distance and timing of O-O bond formation in catalytic turnover could benefit from additional kinetic data.

inputs: Photosystem II crystals in S1, S2, S3 states

hypotheses.hypothesis: An additional oxygen ligand (OX/O6) is inserted into the Mn4Ca cluster during S3 state formation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: OX observed as distinct peak in high-resolution maps ligating to Mn1 and Ca

hypotheses.hypothesis: The O-O bond forms within the S3 state
hypotheses.result: Contradicted: OX-O5 distance of ~2.1 Å indicates weak interaction; O-O bond likely forms during S3→S0 transition

title: Extracellular-matrix mediated stresses spatially bias myoblast fusion and myotube growth

comments: The coupling of active nematic organization with ECM-mediated stress provides an elegant mechanobiological model, though the sufficiency of nematic defects versus intrinsic fusion machinery alone remains to be tested.

hypotheses.result: Confirmed: fusion preferentially occurs at +1/2 defects with high compressive stress

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fusion events create feedback that increases mechanical stress
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: fusion-driven myotube growth increases nematogen length and stress magnitude
